Findings.Title: Model grade verifies a declaration, not the actual reviewer runtime
Findings.Defect: The remaining part of R2-F2 / round-1 F8 is unresolved: the acceptance checks never compare the declared model/effort with the model/effort of the completed reviewer's live execution.
Evidence: request_meta reads hv_request_meta supplied by the runner; verdict_block, verdict_binding, verdict_match and reviewer_turn now bind the verdict and the MCP record, but none reads turn_context or equivalent execution metadata.

A run whose request header says gpt-6-astra/max but whose actual runtime is another model/effort can satisfy all seven listed checks. The plan's own HV protocol at plan:228 explicitly says to verify live rollout metadata and disallows other executions.
Findings.SpecificChange: Add an explicit live-runtime check, tied to the completed reviewer's execution/session and the stored reviewer turn; compare actual model and effort to the configured values. Preserve the new parsed-verdict and complete-claim checks. Name a negative test with correct launch metadata but wrong actual turn_context, and update both contracts, error details, activity and sequence paths. This uses receipt validation; it does not add an HV pipeline.
Findings.Regression: Round 3 fixed parsed verdict binding, scores/findings equality and coverage, and reviewer-turn storage, but left the live-execution part of R2-F2 unimplemented.

Findings.Title: Independence rule excludes every Codex-authored response from the default grader
Findings.Defect: The new check requires both a different MCP session and a different agent name. With ModelGrader.AgentName=Codex, an independently launched Codex gpt-6-astra reviewer can never grade a response whose Agent is Codex.
Evidence: The default grader is Codex; reviewer_turn requires the reviewer's session agent to equal it.

reviewer_independent requires that same agent to differ from response.Agent, and the named test explicitly refuses the same agent. A Codex response therefore always gets 422, even from a genuinely separate reviewer session.
Findings.SpecificChange: Define independence by distinct review execution/session and the actual configured grader execution, allowing two independent Codex sessions. Keep refusal of the producing or reviewed session. Add Codex-producer / independent-Codex-reviewer acceptance and same-session rejection cases.
Findings.Regression: Regression introduced by the new R2-F2 reviewer_independent fix.

Findings.Title: Flat PowerShell builder payloads cannot bind the typed REPL methods
Findings.Defect: The new generic builder/descriptor rule returns the request DTO's fields at the top level and forwards them unchanged to a client method that accepts a complex request/query parameter. That is not the live REPL binding contract.
Evidence: BuildPackageAsync(BuildAgentContextPackageRequest) needs one request object, whereas New-McpAgentContextBuildPackageParams is required to emit sessionId, agent, requestId, queryText, focusRefs and other DTO fields directly.

BindArguments matches dictionary keys to method parameter names; absent required parameter names throw Missing required parameter. It does not synthesize a request object from flat DTO fields. The same mismatch affects submit, grade, retrieve and other complex DTO methods.
AgentResponseTrustDecision is now defined at stateless:250, resolving that portion of R2-F11.
Findings.SpecificChange: Specify each typed method's actual parameter names and the exact REPL envelope, including nesting such as request={...}, query={...}, and separate route ids. Either make builders/descriptors produce that envelope or define the mapping in the PowerShell core. Validate every generated payload through the real GenericClientPassthrough binder, not just a fixture that accepts flat keys, and keep the two documents identical.
Findings.Regression: R2-F11 is partially fixed but not resolved; the newly precise output rule exposes the binding incompatibility.

Findings.Title: Classic Cline hook command is still rejected by the real core
Findings.Defect: The classic Cline command still passes -HookName UserPromptSubmit, while the core accepts user-prompt-submit. The newly planned HostEvent mapping does not include classic Cline or change this command.
Evidence: The current ValidateSet includes user-prompt-submit, not UserPromptSubmit.
A read-only negative invocation of the literal command reached only PowerShell parameter binding and exited 1 with Cannot validate argument on parameter HookName; no hook body ran.
The new AC-008 maps only cline-v2 beforeRun/afterRun and opencode chat.message/session.idle.
Findings.SpecificChange: Change the classic Cline command to the canonical -HookName user-prompt-submit, or explicitly add and specify its HostEvent mapping. Add a test of the literal classic Cline registration command against the real binder.
Findings.Regression: Residual R2-F6. The TypeScript HostEvent and ParamsFromStdin additions fix the earlier missing-parameter design for their named paths, but not this classic path.

Findings.Title: Logic-free adapter drops invocation context and cannot implement OpenCode hooks
Findings.Defect: The transport sends tool arguments alone, although the approved binding requires the separate host ToolContext. It also omits shell.env and specifies returning hook JSON where the real OpenCode hook API requires mutation of an output parameter.
Evidence: Cline-v2 execute(input, toolContext) and OpenCode execute(args, context) have separate context arguments; OpenCode ToolContext.sessionID is not a tool argument. The proposed Invoke-McpPlugin command forwards only args, so two host conversations with identical args lose their distinct session keys.
The host table promises _context.sessionID and shell.env -> MCP_HOST_SESSION_KEY, but AC-008 rejects every event except the four enumerated ones; shell.env is not among them.

OpenCode chat.message(input, output) and shell.env(input, output) return Promise<void>. chat.message's message/parts are in output; shell.env's env is an output object. A single unchanged event object and a parsed return value do not implement these signatures.
Findings.SpecificChange: Define an opaque transport for the complete host invocation (arguments plus separate host context, and both input/output hook parameters) to the PowerShell core, with exact parameters on both platforms. Add shell.env and the required application of the core's returned output to the host's output object as mechanical adapter glue. Test two concurrent host sessions with identical tool args, actual host hook signatures, prompt/message forwarding, and shell environment propagation against the real entry-point binders.
Findings.Regression: Round 3's exact forwarding specification leaves approved A/B session binding unimplementable; the preserved AC text alone does not preserve the behavior.

Findings.Title: Phase A/B activities contradict their approved contracts
Findings.Defect: Several complete-activity claims are false even though Mermaid syntax is valid: terminal enrichment is refused, system queue entries are miscounted, withdrawn unsupported-session closes remain blocking, and bulk submit bypasses the completion gate.
Evidence: TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard rejects a terminal write changing any field before classification runs; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC003 expressly permits omitted-status enrichment and review writes. BindVerbToTurn's explicit-id branch requires a known open turn before it can reach its terminal class/review exception.

ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord compares popAll count only with queued request entries, although every enqueue, including system entries, takes a queue position (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-006 and the named interleaving cases).

EvaluateStopGate sends every withdrawn in-progress turn directly to a block before considering unsupported-session or outage close capture; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 and its named withdrawn-before-delivery case require the captured close to turn that block into a warning.

SubmitSessionLogCommand's activity and sequence go straight to insertion/merge/transaction save, with no CompletionGate or atomic rejection path. The policy and FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC005 require that gate on submit and whole-submission rejection.
Findings.SpecificChange: Make the guard distinguish forbidden status/content replacement from approved omitted-status enrichment; allow explicit terminal targets for the approved class/review verbs; count all queue entries and withdraw only request entries; test captured-close warning eligibility before blocking withdrawn turns; and draw the completion gate plus its error/rollback path on bulk submit. Mirror corrections in response sequences and use existing named discriminating cases as the branch checklist.
Findings.Regression: These are merge/diagram fidelity failures, not a request to change the approved A/B substance. R2-F7's nonce-code and Unstarted fixes themselves remain resolved.

Findings.Title: HV requests containing terminal responses can never complete
Findings.Defect: HV creation snapshots every response in the turn range, but model grading refuses Rejected and Superseded responses. Completion requires every item to receive a model grade; there is no alternate item disposition or request cancellation.
Evidence: Create a valid range containing one Rejected response: the request is created Open, its sole item is ungraded, every RecordModelGrade call returns 409 agent_context_response_not_gradable, and Completed is unreachable.
Filtering at creation alone would not fix a response that becomes Rejected or Superseded after the request is created.
Findings.SpecificChange: Define a complete per-item lifecycle for terminal responses and transitions during review. For example, permit an audit-only model grade that cannot revive terminal trust, or give terminal items an explicit completed disposition counted toward request completion. Specify response fields, errors, diagrams and tests for pre-existing and mid-review rejection/supersession.
Findings.Regression: No regression attribution; found in the current merged contract.

Findings.Title: A transaction alone does not serialize concurrent trust decisions
Findings.Defect: The plan asserts that inserting a grade and deciding trust in the same transaction makes concurrent writes safe, but defines no isolation/locking/version-and-retry protocol. This does not guarantee that stored response status reflects the latest committed grade pair.
Evidence: The storage contract explicitly says there are no concurrency tokens; no per-response serializable transaction, durable lock or compare-and-swap is specified.

Permitted interleaving: existing deterministic Pass, response Grading; transaction A inserts deterministic Fail; transaction B inserts model Pass and reads the old deterministic Pass; A commits; B commits Trusted. The final latest deterministic grade fails while the response is trusted.
The live SessionLogService.cs:156 explicitly selects IsolationLevel.Serializable for its own different operation; the new context contract makes no such selection.
Findings.SpecificChange: Specify serialization of grade insertion and trust/status changes per response for SQLite, PostgreSQL and SQL Server, with conflict/deadlock retry semantics. Apply the same ordering to reject/stale/supersede races. Add a forced interleaving test that would produce the invalid Trusted state under a nonserialized implementation.
Findings.Regression: No regression attribution; found in the current merged contract.

Findings.Title: Response idempotency ignores package, claims and evidence
Findings.Defect: The response contract says key reuse with different inputs is a conflict, but both replay and concurrent-insert paths compare only ContentSha256. Identical answer text with different package, agent/model, claims or evidence silently returns the old response.
Evidence: SubmitAgentResponseRequest includes packageId, agent, model, effort, invocationMode, contentFormat, claims and evidence in addition to content and idempotencyKey.
Both activity branches return 200 existing/winner response on the same content hash. ContentSha256 hashes the answer content, not the submission inputs; root ids are copied from the original package.
Findings.SpecificChange: Define a canonical immutable submission fingerprint covering the package/root identity and all grading-relevant fields, store it, and use it on replay and unique-index collision. Return 409 on any differing input. Add same-content/different-package and same-content/different-claims/evidence cases.
Findings.Regression: No regression attribution; found in the current merged contract.

Findings.Title: Staleness misses response evidence and standalone trusted retrieval
Findings.Defect: A response's Requirement/File evidence is linked as supports, but staleness checks only depends_on and derived_from. Evidence added by the response outside its package can change without invalidating trust. Standalone retrieval also has no staleness evaluation boundary.
Evidence: A response can cite a code file absent from its package, pass both grades, and become Trusted. Submission adds a supports link. After the file changes, EvaluateStaleness ignores that link, so even a subsequent package build can keep the response trusted.

Evaluation triggers are before package construction and after requirement updates/deletes. RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery can return a previously Trusted response after a file/profile/rule change without running evaluation.
Findings.SpecificChange: Define which evidence forms an authoritative dependency and record/check its hash (including response-added evidence). Ensure every trusted retrieval validates freshness or consumes an atomically maintained freshness/version barrier. Add direct-retrieve-after-file-change and changed-response-only-evidence tests, preserving rejected/stale artifacts for audit.
Findings.Regression: No regression attribution; found in the current merged contract.

Findings.Title: Relational retrieval ranks against request context that its request cannot identify
Findings.Defect: RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery promises to rank relationships to the request's requirements, TODO and turn, but AgentContextRetrieveRequest has no session/request/package/focus references. WorkspacePath plus free queryText cannot identify that relationship neighborhood.
Evidence: The entire DTO is queryText, kinds, limit, trustedOnly, preferGraphRag.
The handler accepts only WorkspacePath and that DTO and is independently exposed through REST/MCP/client/REPL/plugins; no bound turn context is part of this contract.
Findings.SpecificChange: Add explicit request/focus identity or define and validate a separate bound context argument for both external retrieval and the builder's internal call. Specify unknown/cross-workspace reference errors and propagate the exact fields through every surface and diagram. Test identical query text with two different turn/requirement neighborhoods.
Findings.Regression: No regression attribution; found in the current merged contract.

Findings.Title: Stateless mode has no contract for removing host conversation history
Findings.Defect: The only specified host operation is injecting additional/system context, followed by the assertion that history is absent. No host operation, adapter input/output contract, or capability check removes/replaces the conversation history for the model invocation.
Evidence: RunStatelessInvocation checks whether the host can refuse a prompt, but not whether it can construct a fresh model request or replace its message list.

The activity and sequence say no history without defining the mechanism. The plugin test asks for no-history injection but could pass by inspecting only the added context; that does not establish what messages the host sends to the model.
This is an absent contract, not a claim that no supported host can implement stateless execution.
Findings.SpecificChange: Specify the actual history-exclusion operation per supported host (fresh invocation or authoritative message-list replacement), the complete model input boundary, and capability-based refusal/limitation where unavailable. Add a host-level test with a sentinel prior turn proving it is absent from the actual model request while the package and current request are present.
Findings.Regression: No regression attribution; found in the current merged contract.
